Specifical corrective action CA-8134, opened due to|- customer loads impacted as a result of the temperature within the aeration room falling below the minimum temperature for more than 30 minutes. Two root causes have been identified as part of the CAPA Investigation. Specifically, A.Laboratory control procedures are not followed: -During review of electronic data for [redacted] USP API, we observed multiple unreported sample injections prior to or after the official reported sample injections for Related Substances and Assay by HPLC testing that were not documented in laboratory batch records. API batches involved; - [redacted] included batch numbers. Batches oe were approved by QA and shipped to the U.S. market. -During the current inspection we requested your firm to perform calculations for all unreported Related Substances and Assay injections, where at least one batch, [redacted] revealed an unreported injection with an OOS result. Specifically, on 12/20/2024, your analyst injected a blank and single injection for sample [redacted], with calculations during the current inspection resulting in OOS for assay, with calculated result a [redacted] % versus specification of [redacted] %. The official reported result documented in your laboratory batch records for [redacted] was performed on 12/22/2024, with reported result as [redacted] %. This batch was shipped to the U.S. Market. -When we asked one of your analysts why they performed an unreported injection prior to the official injection, the analyst stated that the owner of the firm provided the sample and asked them to perform the test. Review of this analyst's training record revealed no laboratory training on performing any testing operations, including chromatography testing, no cGMP training, and no data integrity training. -After discussion of these deficiencies with your QC Manager, he stated that "for export purpose we check for confirmation again and again." -Furthermore, we observed that your firm appears to be performing arbitrary in-process sampling. Per your firm's QC Manager, your firm does not always perform in-process sampling, only when the firm's owner provides samples to test. We observed no laboratory batch records or calculations for in-process sampling, no assigned batch numbers in the sample set to in-process samples, and no mention of in-process sampling in batch records. In sample sets reviewed, there is no way of determining what batch numbers of [redacted] USP API were tested from the electronic data. Your firm's QC Manager stated that they did not know what batches were tested. -Consequently, QA and QC do not review electronic data, nor does your firm have a procedure for review of electronic data for the [redacted] standalone HPLC and [redacted] standalone GC equipment. Similarly, your firm does not have a procedure for sample set and sample naming conventions. B.During our walkthrough of the QC laboratory on January 19, 2026, a discarded printout was found in a trash bin. After review, your QC Manager stated that the printout documented a Loss on Drying (LOD) test for [redacted] raw material, AR. No. [redacted] dated January 18, 2026. Per your QC Manager, the test was performed in duplicate by an analyst by accident. Review of the discarded printout revealed that the analyst performed the weighing of the first LOD bottle, then performed the weighing of the second LOD bottle. After completing the second bottle, the analyst re-weighed the first bottle again, mistakenly believing the first bottle had not been weighed yet. The weight recorded for this re-weighing was [redacted] g, while the reported initial test weight was (4) g, indicating the same bottle was weighed twice. However, instead of initiating a laboratory incident as required by your procedures, your analyst discarded the second printout without documentation. During the inspection, your firm acknowledged the discrepancy; however, as of the closeout of the inspection, your firm failed to initiate a formal investigation. Furthermore, our review found zero incidents have been initiated within your QC unit over at least the last three years, despite routine analytical testing.

Specifically, e Corrective and preventive actions are not initiated in accordance with established procedures. Per 13 Corrective and Preventive Actions Rev 19 08/14/2025, page 4, section 2.2, review of nonconformance records can result in a decision of corrective action required; when the nonconformance evaluation indicates a recurring or systemic issue, a new CAPA will be initiated and linked to the nonconformance. Per 12 Control of Non-conforming product Rev 27 11/07/2025 page 3 section 3.2, a risk assessment to determine the need for generating a corrective action is performed b, then a Corrective Action 1s required. However, in 3 of 11 customer nonconformance records reviewed (CN 140, 145, and 171), the risk assessment documented an RPN value ofi but no corrective action was initiated. e Risk assessment performed to determine CAPA initiation is inadequate. Per 12 Control of Non- conforming product Rev 27 11/07/2025 page 3 section 3.2, a multidisciplinary team, using predefined tables, shall determine the value of the nonconformity’s occurrence, detection and severity. Per the occurrence table, a ranking of Bis given to nonconformances that has not previously occurred. However, per vendor nonconformance NC VN-0090, on 06/25/2024, foreign matter or contaminants were identified on 4) lot [redacted]. The same nonconformance was identified in bo - an - for the same part and the recurrence was within 180 days. Per 12 Control of Non-conforming product Rev 27 11/07/2025 page 3 section 3.2, this is an occurrence ranking off. If the risk assessment of NC VN-0129 was calculated using an occurrence score of i. the resulting RPN value off would have required the initiation of a CAPA. e Corrective and preventive action root cause investigation is inadequate. Per 13 Corrective and Preventive Actions Rev 19 08/14/2025, page 4 section 2.3, a root cause investigation will be performed which will guide the development of a CAPA plan to eliminate and prevent recurrence of the nonconformity. However, in 2 of 11 CAPAs reviewed, a root cause investigation did not adequately identify the root cause. For example: e Per CA 138 on 04/01/2024 the calibration sticker for theOr a torque driver was missing and master torque driver used to check drivers used in production waseG past due for calibration. Per the root cause investigation, there is no system in place for calibration or verification of torque tools. A corrective action was implemented to. However, the CAPA did not identify why the master torque ver was allowed to be past due for calibration; no corrections were implemented to address this deficiency. The same deficiency of past due calibrations was identified in 02/27/2025 for a multimeter and a force gauge. This deficiency was addressed via CA 147. e Per CA 152 on 04/01/2025, it was identified that screws being used during assembly were screws without [redacted] — instead of the same sized screws with [redacted] Per the root cause investigation, the bill of materials was incorrect and the work instructions were not available. A corrective action was implemented to correct the bill of materials, retrain the staff, and change the layout of the work area to locate [redacted] — screws where required. However, the root cause investigation did not identify cause of the incorrect bill of materials. e Verification of the effectiveness of corrective and preventive actions are not performed in accordance with established procedures. Per 13 Corrective and Preventive Actions Rev 19 08/14/2025 page 4 section 2.4, an effectiveness verification plan is determined to ensure that the precipitating issue triggering the CAPA and identified root causes have been addressed by the CAPA plan actions; specific and measurable outputs of the processes related to the originating issues shall be used to determine the pass/fail status of the effectiveness of the CAPA actions. However, in 5 of 11 CAPAs reviewed (CA 138, 139, 141, 149, 152) the verification of effectiveness plan does not contain measurable outputs of the process to determine a pass/fail status for the effectiveness of the CAPA actions.
